subject: Deployment tradeoffs and cost model request — hosted / dedicated / VPC
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@parallax.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 03 Oct 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Deployment tradeoffs (hosted / dedicated / VPC) + next asks

Hi Sanjay — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Primary goals you shared
- Start with an aggressive pilot for in-app generative recommendations (Q4 launch target)
- Peak concurrency ~180 RPS during business hours, average 2.8M tokens/day today, forecast 8–10M tokens/day in 6 months
- Strong data residency requirement for EU customer data; primary infra US for now but VPC required for some regulated flows

2) Deployment options we discussed (high level)
- Hosted API: fastest path, per-token billing, Redwood-managed model and autoscaling; ideal for initial pilot velocity
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools (monthly commit), predictable throughput and lower per-token economics at scale; useful if sustained high concurrency is required
- Private VPC/on-prem: for regulated EU flow that must stay in-customer network; involves platform licensing + infra ops

3) Asks / what we need from Parallax to model economics accurately
- Historical 30/60/90 day token volumes (by model type if available) — cc. procurement if you prefer a spreadsheet drop
- Peak concurrency windows (per region) and percent of requests that require EU residency
- Typical request/response length (input tokens / output tokens) by major endpoint (recommendations, chat, batch scoring)

4) Next steps (proposed)
- You upload the usage snapshot to the Drive folder I shared (or send the CSV attached to this thread).
- We run a short costing exercise comparing three scenarios: hosted (per-token with burst), dedicated reserved commit (1yr and 3yr), and private VPC (license + infra estimate).
- Proposed workshop: Thursday, Oct 11, 10:00–11:30 PT — technical + finance stakeholders (we'll bring an initial cost model).

Attached: redwood_model_costing.xlsx (blank workbook with scenario tabs) — please confirm if you want us to prefill with your numbers.

Evelyn

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Deployment tradeoffs (hosted / dedicated / VPC) + next asks

Thanks Evelyn — appreciate the recap. I uploaded a quick usage snapshot into the Drive folder and attached a CSV (parallax_current_usage.csv) to this reply. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 2.8M tokens/day is current baseline for internal beta; the 8–10M forecast includes new public-facing features and a marketing push.
- ~22% of requests will need EU residency (GDPR reasons) — those are mostly enterprise customers.
- Average request size: 120 tokens in, 280 tokens out for recommendation endpoint; chat is more variable (300–700 tokens).

On economics: we need a clear illustration of the point where dedicated reserved capacity becomes cheaper than hosted per-token pricing. Also concerned about commit flexibility — our traffic could ramp faster than a 12mo commit allows.

Can you prefill the spreadsheet with our numbers? Procurement would like to see a 12-month vs 36-month commit comparison and an option with mixed mode: Hosted for non-sensitive traffic + VPC for EU flows.

Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Product, Parallax AI

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>

Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@parallax.ai>
Date: Thu, 04 Oct 2028 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Deployment tradeoffs (hosted / dedicated / VPC) + next asks

Evelyn / Rishi — I reviewed the CSV Sanjay uploaded and sketched a quick back-of-envelope. Key inputs I used are in the attached redwood_model_costing.xlsx (tab: initial_BE) — I dropped notes on assumptions in column headers. Summary (very rough):

- Hosted (per-token): with forecasted 9M tokens/day, estimate $0.00025 per token effective (API + model costs with caching assumptions) = ~$6750/day; high day-to-day variability but no commit required.
- Dedicated (reserved 1yr): assuming a 2x headroom GPU pool to handle peaks, effective per-token math comes to ~$0.00012/token = ~$3240/day (sustained efficiency at scale). 3yr commit improves further.
- Private VPC: platform licensing (~$30k/mo) + infra (customer-managed GPUs) — economics depend heavily on infra amortization; for Parallax's forecast, mixed-mode (hosted + VPC for EU) looks promising: host non-EU traffic, reserve capacity for core engine handling peak global traffic, VPC for EU-sensitive flows.

Open questions we need to finalize the model:
- Concurrency-to-GPU mapping: need peak RPS per model variant (not just global RPS)
- Cache hit expectations (percent of tokens served from prefix/KV cache) — greatly impacts hosted per-token cost
- Expected hourly distribution (how spiky is traffic) — affects required headroom and autoscale behavior

I also highlighted an approach to flexible commits: 9-mo ramped commit + burst credit pool — we can model that as a transitional option.

Vanessa
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
